item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Severe rainfall and flood warnings issued for central Greece and western Turkey
item.description:
Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expected

Heavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms. During a particularly intense thunderstorm in Antalya, a coastal city in the south-west of Turkey, the formation of a tornado resulted in the deaths of four construction workers on Tuesday. Authorities in Greece and Turkey have released severe rainfall and flooding warnings, as a further 100-150mm (nearly 4-6in) of rain is expected this week in central Greece and western parts of Turkey, with locally higher totals possible.

Travelling eastwards towards south Asia, strong winds and heavy rainfall have swept across the Indian regions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall. With wind gusts in excess of 85mph (140km/h) and rainfall totals in some regions exceeding 200mm, the severe storm has prompted mass evacuations of more than 180,000 people, as well as widespread disruption to energy and transport infrastructure. The cyclone will weaken as it continues to traverse northwards over the coming days, though will continue to deliver heavy rain to parts of northern and central India as it does so.

item.description:
Turkey nominates OSCE chief Sinirlioglu for UN's top job

Turkey has nominated Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, leader of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), to be the next UN secretary-general, the country's official Anadolu news agency reported on Saturday.

A nomination letter dated Friday from Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been submitted to the presidents of the UN General Assembly and the Security Council, Anadolu said, citing Turkish foreign ministry sources.

The move came after a deadlock in the selection process, with the latest straw poll at the UN Security Council held on Friday returning an inconclusive outcome, the sources told the news agency.

The outgoing secretary-general, Antonio Guterres of Portugal, ends his second five-year term on December 31.

Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 available in the Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided.

Once a candidate clears those bars, their name will go to the General Assembly of all UN members for confirmation. 

Report by AFP

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Hormuz shipping traffic remains 70% below pre-war levels, UKMTO says
item.description:
Hormuz shipping traffic remains 70% below pre-war levels, UKMTO says

Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains 70 percent below pre-conflict levels, with vessels continuing to face attacks, navigation interference and security risks across the Gulf, according to a weekly assessment by the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

A total of 277 vessel transits were recorded in the strait during the seven days to October 28, comprising 155 inbound and 122 outbound movements. The combined figure, which includes automatic identification system (AIS) observations and US-reported facilitated transits, was approximately 70 percent below pre-conflict levels.

UKMTO said AIS-observed transits increased to 64 from 47 the previous week, while US-reported facilitated movements remained broadly stable. The US Naval Cooperation and Guidance for Shipping (NCAGS) estimates that about 80% of transits through the strait involve energy carriers.

Most vessels broadcasting AIS continued to use the Iranian route, although UKMTO reported an increase in traffic along the southern route.

The maritime monitoring body said it had recorded 88 incidents in the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began on February 28, with the data suggesting at least 35 attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz in October, making it the worst month for attacks since the start of the war.

March was the second-worst month, with about 30 attacks, according to UKMTO data.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Morning update
item.description:
Morning update

Good Morning Middle East Eye readers,

If you are just joining us, here are key developments from across the region and beyond:

*Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said that four oil tankers had caught fire and exploded while attempting to use what it described as unauthorised routes through the Strait of Hormuz.

*US President Donald Trump has said that talks with Iran are ongoing, and that Tehran wants to talk, while reiterating that Washington was not engaged in a "typical war".

*Saudi-led coalition forces have intercepted and destroyed a drone each over Saudi Arabia's Riyadh, Eastern Province and southern region. 

*More than 530 Palestinian families have been forced from their homes in Hebron in the occupied West Bank during a citywide lockdown by Israeli forces, Al Jazeera has reported.

* A Palestinian was killed in an Israeli air strike in central Nuseirat, while another person died from injuries sustained in a previous air attack on Gaza City. 

*An Israeli air attack has targeted the town of Kfar Tebnit in the Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon, Al Jazeera reported.

* Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi has criticised Germany for supporting Israel-US war on Iran last year and now complaining the conflict has added has added more than 100 billion euros ($112bn) to Europe’s energy costs.

*London Metropolitan Police has warned that anyone planning to attend a demonstration in support of Palestine Action in the vicinity of the US Embassy on Saturday will face arrest "as part of a robust policing operation".

* Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains 70 percent below pre-conflict levels, with vessels continuing to face attacks, navigation interference and security risks across the Gulf, according to a weekly assessment by the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

*German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said that Germany was working to bring Iran war to an end as soon as possible as the conflict has added more than 100 billion euros ($112bn) to Europe’s energy costs over the past eight months.

* Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan has met with his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers meeting in the US.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Oil spills from tankers attacked by Iran in Hormuz reach UAE coastline, report says
item.description:
Oil spills from tankers attacked by Iran in Hormuz reach UAE coastline, report says

Oil spills from tankers attacked by Iran near the Strait of Hormuz have reached the UAE coastline, prompting beach closures in three emirates and raising concerns about marine life, the Financial Times reported.

The first spill to reach the coast left dark slicks along beaches, with authorities closing affected areas in Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah. The UAE environment ministry said it was coordinating cleanup operations and urged fishermen to avoid polluted areas.

Marine monitor Windward recorded 12 spills between July and September, including one that spread across an area of 2,000 square kilometres off Oman. Satellite imagery also showed an oil slick near Ras Al Khaimah. Experts warned that turtles, dolphins, seabirds and other marine species could be affected.

Authorities have not identified the leaking vessel, but marine security experts cited by the FT said it was the Chinese-owned supertanker Gem No. 2, hit off Sharjah more than two weeks ago.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] ‘The last fortress’: historic Athens cafe closes as countercultural area gentrifies
item.description:
Mouria coffeehouse unable to renew lease in Exarchia, known for leftwing solidarity, resistance and radicalism

It has been the hangout of writers, artists, poets and politicians, doctors and lawyers, radicals and revolutionaries for as long as anyone can remember. And for 44 years, Christos Vanas, the proprietor of Mouria, has let them all in.

Every day at 7am, the taciturn former waiter has been the first man to step inside the historic cafe in Exarchia, the heart of leftwing Athens. It is a ritual he has kept punctiliously, opening up the famous gathering place before he himself has had his first coffee.
